plain: To make something last longer; to drag it out

webster.text: To draw out or lengthen in time; to continue; to prolong; as, to protract an argument; to protract a discussion; to protract a war or a negotiation.

example.quote: This new system will protract the time in which the ability of the state will enable them to pay off their debt, because all the funds of the state will be transferred to the general government, except those which arise from internal taxes.
example.cite: Brutus XIII, New York Journal, Feb. 21, 1788
